# RustyNES v2.7.4 — "Pocket"

The fifth release of the audit line that [ADR 0041](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/adr/0041-hardware-release-is-v3.0.0.md) put between v2.6.23 and the SuperStation One core (**v3.0.0**). It works from the frontend audit in [`docs/audits/`](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/README.md), and its subject is the two mobile apps: what happens to them when a phone does what phones do — backgrounds them, takes a call, loses a headset, runs out of memory mid-write, or hits a bug.

All 30 mobile findings were checked against the code before anything changed. Four were refuted, one was deferred, and one turned out much worse than reported; every verdict is in the [frontend ledger](https://github.com/doublegate/RustyNES/blob/main/docs/audits/frontend-disposition.md). One fix is in the emulation core and affects every platform, so **AccuracyCoin 144/144** and **nestest** were re-measured on the release tree, and the full `--features test-roms` workspace suite passes **2,716 tests, 0 failed**.

**Most of this release needs a real phone to confirm.** Every iOS change is written but not compiled on this project's Linux machines, and the Android lifecycle and audio changes need a device; both are on the maintainer's per-platform device checklist, which gates this release's merge. The Android battery-save path was run on the emulator. **The MiSTer sibling does not change, and no hardware has run any bitstream**; the board session is v2.9.2.

## A bug no longer closes the app

The Android and iOS libraries were built to stop the process on any internal error. The audit asked for error containment at the native entry points, assuming the rest of the bridge was already protected; neither held, because in that build mode nothing can contain an error — not the new guards, and not the ones the binding generator already puts around every call. So one bug anywhere ended the app with no save and no report.

The mobile libraries now build with a profile that recovers (`release-mobile`), every native entry point contains a failure, and if one happens the game keeps running, any netplay session is ended, and the app shows a message. Measured cost: about 18% more native code on arm64, and no measurable difference in frame time.

## Battery saves on the phones

v2.7.3 gave the desktop in-game saves. Android and iOS now keep them too, with the same rules: only cartridges whose header says they have a battery, a save loaded before the game's first frame, and a save file that cannot be used left untouched rather than overwritten. On the Android emulator a test cartridge that counts its own power-ons read 1, 2 and 3 across three force-closed launches.

## Android

- **The game pauses when the app leaves the screen**, and the app now takes part in audio focus: it goes quiet for a call, ducks under a navigation prompt, and hands the audio back while paused. Picture-in-picture keeps playing.
- **Saves survive a dying phone.** Save states, achievement progress, the recent-games list, the library and per-game settings are written so that an interrupted write leaves the previous copy, not a truncated one.
- Opening a game and the save-state screen no longer do their file work on the interface thread, where a slow cloud-backed file could freeze the app.
- The GPU renderer recovers after a slow screen teardown instead of staying black, and no longer wakes hundreds of times a second while idle. The game screen no longer rebuilds all of its interface on every frame.

## iOS

- **Audio stays in step.** The iOS sound output had no rate control; it now holds a steady 50 ms buffer, starts from a full one, and comes back after the system's media services reset. Unplugging headphones no longer leaves the game frozen until the app is sent to the background.
- **A smoother picture.** The display runs at 60 Hz with exactly one emulated frame per refresh; the previous 120 Hz link showed a frame twice or skipped one every few seconds.
- **iCloud save states are not lost.** Uploads finish when the app is backgrounded, a save whose upload failed is retried instead of shown as synced, and an older save from one device can no longer overwrite a newer one from another.
- A swipe off the bottom of the controls no longer sends the app home; video filters pause while the device is hot; opening a ROM from another app while a game is running no longer freezes the screen; joining an online game no longer freezes the interface during the address lookup.

## Every platform

- **Touch and gamepad input never wait for the emulator.** A button press waited for the current frame, a netplay rollback or a script to finish.
- **A failed save-state load leaves the game as it was.** A state rejected partway through left a half-restored machine that then kept running — on the desktop and in RetroArch too.
- Leaving netplay or logging out of RetroAchievements no longer freezes the app for up to 10-30 seconds when the server is unreachable.
- ROM files over 16 MiB are refused before they are copied.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| AccuracyCoin (RAM decoder) | 144 / 144, 0 fail, 0 not run |
| nestest | pass |
| `--features test-roms` workspace suite | 154 suites, 2,716 passed, 0 failed |
| fmt, clippy (default, `scripting,hd-pack`, `retroachievements`, `av-record`, `script-ipc`, `full`, both wasm32), `cargo doc -D warnings`, `no_std` build | clean |
| Android: Gradle, both flavours, and the app's first JVM unit tests | compile; 7 tests pass |
| Android emulator | battery-save boot counter 1, 2, 3 across force-closed launches |
| iOS-only Rust (`scripts/ios-host-typecheck.sh`, now in CI) | compiles on Linux against the real audio library; 16 tests pass |
| Red first | every fix a test can observe was pinned by a test that fails on v2.7.3 (the netplay teardown test waited 10.06 s) |
| Mutations | each such fix reverted in turn and caught; the few that are expected not to be caught (a performance-only change, a redundant second safety check) say so at the site |

**Not under automated test:** every Swift change; on Android the render-thread restart, the frame-rebuild scoping, the background pause, audio focus and the idle wake-up. The maintainer's device checklist covers each; anything it could not confirm is listed in the release's known issues.

**Deferred:** removing the per-frame copy of the picture through the mobile bridge (about 15 MB/s) is a performance change and moves to v2.7.5 with the others.

**Next:** v2.7.5 is performance and API hygiene, each change kept only if it measures faster and changes nothing.
